core: JavaScript array elements, zero-based indexing, and length

claims.claim: JavaScript arrays are collections with zero-based numeric indexes and a length property.
Bracket notation can access or assign an array element by index.
push appends values and returns the new array length, while pop removes and returns the final element.
push, pop, shift, and unshift mutate the target array.
A const binding cannot be reassigned, but an array referenced by it can be mutated.
Array.isArray determines whether a supplied value is an array.
